review.summary: The Hydra Mist launch post draft requires significant revisions to align with Dewpoint's brand guidelines and regulatory standards. Please address the prohibited copy, imagery, color palette, and missing ingredient disclosures before resubmission.

flags.issue: Use of prohibited drug claims like 'Heals' and 'Clinically proven', and the term 'anti-aging'.
flags.suggestion: Remove prohibited terms and replace with approved phrasing like 'Supports the skin barrier'; include study citations for timeframe claims.

citations.quote: We don't use "anti-aging". Just describe what it does: "barrier support for cold, dry air".
citations.author: Sofia Reyes

citations.quote: "Heals" is a drug claim. We can't say it. "Supports the skin barrier" is the approved phrasing, and no timeframe claims without a study reference.
citations.author: Sofia Reyes

observations: [Compliance] Prohibited drug claims: the word 'Heals' is forbidden; use 'Supports the skin barrier' instead. As of October 2025, Sofia Reyes (Regulatory & Claims Lead) has mandated that 'anti-aging' is also prohibited in web banner copy, requiring the use of 'barrier support for cold, dry air' instead. As of July 2026, Sofia Reyes requires the exact wording 'Broad Spectrum SPF 30' for SPF claims and explicitly forbids the phrase 'all-day protection'. Timeframe claims must include a study reference; as of December 2025, this includes citing the source for any statistical claims (e.g., 50% skin barrier improvement) in small type on the relevant slide. Before/after imagery is prohibited as it implies guaranteed results and risks ad rejection; use single texture close-up images and include the disclaimer 'individual results vary'. This disclaimer must be presented in small type.

flags.suggestion: Remove before/after panels and replace with a single close-up image of real, unretouched skin texture.

citations.quote: No before/after imagery. It implies guaranteed results and we've already had an ad rejected for it. Use a single week-4 texture close-up with "individual results vary".
citations.author: Sofia Reyes

evidence.text: [Colour] Dewpoint color palette: bone #F5F0EA, clay #C9A58A, stone #8C8279, ink #2B2826.

[Colour] Dewpoint requires a warm color palette; ice-blue (#DDEBF5) and cool grey-blue (#C9D3DB) are prohibited as they feel too clinical. As of October 2025, Lukas Brandt (Head of Brand) has mandated a shift for the 'Website banner: winter barrier kit' project, requiring a palette of warm neutrals (bone and stone) as the base and clay as an accent, while explicitly prohibiting orange. This replaces the previous clinical/cool aesthetic request for this project. Additionally, as of April 2026, Lukas Brandt prohibits the use of pink florals in design assets, noting they are overused by beauty brands.
[Colour] Dewpoint prohibits the use of gradients in design assets, as they are perceived as cheap and techy; flat colors are required.
[Compliance] Dewpoint brand identity is warm, calm, and radically transparent.
[Imagery] Dewpoint brand rule: Never retouch skin texture in imagery; pores, freckles, and fine lines must remain visible.

[Copy] Dewpoint requires a maximum of twenty words per slide and strictly one idea per slide for carousel projects, as mandated by Lukas Brandt (Head of Brand) in December 2025 following a rejection of excessive copy.
[Layout] Dewpoint requires final approval from Amara Nwosu (Founder) for all project design drafts.
[Compliance] Dewpoint brand positioning: not a pharmacy, not a spa.
[Typography] Dewpoint prohibits the use of script typography in design assets, as mandated by Lukas Brandt (Head of Brand) in April 2026.

[Copy] Dewpoint brand rule: Never promise 'flawless' skin; use 'Healthy skin' or 'her skin, supported' as approved alternatives. Amara Nwosu (Founder) confirmed 'her skin, supported' as approved copy for the Mother's Day gift post in April 2026.

[Compliance] Prohibited drug claims: the word 'Heals' is forbidden; use 'Supports the skin barrier' instead. As of October 2025, Sofia Reyes (Regulatory & Claims Lead) has mandated that 'anti-aging' is also prohibited in web banner copy, requiring the use of 'barrier support for cold, dry air' instead. As of July 2026, Sofia Reyes requires the exact wording 'Broad Spectrum SPF 30' for SPF claims and explicitly forbids the phrase 'all-day protection'. Timeframe claims must include a study reference; as of December 2025, this includes citing the source for any statistical claims (e.g., 50% skin barrier improvement) in small type on the relevant slide. Before/after imagery is prohibited as it implies guaranteed results and risks ad rejection; use single texture close-up images and include the disclaimer 'individual results vary'. This disclaimer must be presented in small type.

[Imagery] Dewpoint brand rule: Imagery must show more of the person and use natural light to avoid a clinical, dermatology-textbook aesthetic; tight crops are prohibited. The approved 'Real skin campaign: Instagram' asset features a shoulders-up crop, natural window light, and is unretouched.
